text:
olga: Ledgerly trial ends Tues. Finance flagged a couple weird invoice lines. Can someone sanity-check before we engage legal?
sam.k: I pulled the sanitized sample. They bill: compute-hours, tokenized output, and a separate data-egress line. Also an "activation" waiver credit that offsets part of init fees.
irene: paste the sanitized lines pls. We need to map to our SKU ids.
sam.k: pasted below (sanitized):
```
LEDGERLY ACTIVATE-CREDIT: -1 account @ $150 = -$150.00
LEDGERLY COMPUTE-HOURS: 12.5 hrs @ $18/hr = $225.00
LEDGERLY TOKENS-OUT: 510,432 tokens @ $0.00095/token = $484.91
LEDGERLY EGRESS-GB: 42 GB @ $0.12/GB = $5.04
LEDGERLY SUPPORT-CHAT: 3 msgs @ $5/msg = $15.00
TOTAL = $579.95
```
chris (Ledgerly): Hi all : thanks for the extract. Quick notes: compute-hours are only billed for heavy batch jobs (we flag them via a job type header). Tokens-out counts only generated tokens, not prompt tokens. Egress is actual bytes served from our cache or S3. Activation-credit is a one-time onboarding credit applied on first invoice.
olga: Two asks from procurement: 1) can you emit a machine-readable invoice CSV with sku_id, qty, unit_price, currency, invoice_line_hash? 2) do you support Net60 + PO for enterprise deals?
chris (Ledgerly): We can emit CSV with sku_id and a stable invoice_line_id (not a nested hash, but a UUID per line). Net60 + PO is possible for 12mo commits >= $100k ARR. For smaller deals Net30 or Net45.
irene: How do you define compute-hour buckets? we need to map to our cost model (gpunode.hour vs cpu.hour).
chris (Ledgerly): Compute-hours are GPU-hours (A100-equivalent). We will supply a mapping file that lists equivalent SKU (gpu.a100.hour) so you can translate.
olga: Billing credits: we used a $4k trial credit. Do trial credits reduce the commit threshold or apply as invoice credit on conversion?
chris (Ledgerly): Trial credits are applied as invoice credits on conversion. They don't reduce commit threshold, but we can consider a one-time concession if you push to a 24mo commit.
sam.k: Any early-termination / refund policy? Procurement wants clarity on unused committed credits if we terminate.
chris (Ledgerly): Standard: unused committed spend is credited back as invoice credit pro-rated for the remaining term, minus a 10% early-exit administration fee. Negotiable on large enterprise deals.
irene: Tokenization mismatch has haunted us before. Will you provide a tokenizer or accept Redwood's counts for billing reconciliation?
chris (Ledgerly): We use a subtle variant of BPE; we'll provide a tokenization script. We can accept Redwood's counts if we sign the reconciliation addendum and agree an initial audit window (30 days).
olga: Tax & currency: can you invoice in EUR and include VAT ID for reverse-charge? Also need explicit currency field in CSV.
chris (Ledgerly): Yes on EUR invoicing and VAT reverse-charge with VAT ID field in CSV. Currency and tax fields will be columns.
acct-bot: Reminder : Vendor risk questionnaire outstanding: https://vendor-portal.redwood.com/risk/Ledgerly Assigned to @irene and @legal.team. Due in 4 business days.
olga: One more technical: do you provide a billing webhook or export of usage events (ndjson) so we can auto-ingest into our billing ETL?
chris (Ledgerly): We provide both a daily CSV export and a near-real-time NDJSON webhook (events schema v2). We'll include a schema doc and example payloads.
irene: OK next steps: @chris please upload CSV with sku_ids, provide tokenizer script, show compute->gpu-hour mapping, and confirm Net60+PO conditions in writing. @irene and finance will review the reconciliation addendum and vendor risk. If all looks good we'll request a draft contract with the activation-credit applied and 12mo pricing.
chris (Ledgerly): Will upload today and follow up with a short quote. Happy to do a 15m call if that helps.
olga: Thanks team. If we get the CSV soon I'll run a 30-day cost projection and post results here before EOD.
